caption: Newanforbi v. Macy's Inc. et al.
claims: PC §290.46(j) Violation, Wrongful Termination, FCRA, ICRAA, UCL §17200, IIED, NIED
status: NOT PURSUING — Voluntarily Dismissed. The anticipated registry-based adverse action never occurred: Macy's honored the offer, and Plaintiff worked the position from May 28, 2026 until an unrelated CDCR retaliatory transfer (see Matter 30) made the Stockton job inaccessible on July 2, 2026. No PC §290.46(j) violation ever materialized on these facts.
key_facts: On May 28, 2026, Defendant Macy's Inc., through Recruiter Toni Ashe and Hiring Manager Leticia Villarreal, extended a written job offer to Plaintiff Brendan Ngwa Nforbi for the position of 'Captain, Selling and Support' at Macy's - Stockton Sherwood, 5242 Pacific Ave, MCE 71338, Stockton, CA 95207, San Joaquin County, California. The offer letter, dated May 28, 2026, and signed by Macy's corporate leadership, specified: $21.50/hour; Start Date: May 28, 2026; Position Type: ORA_HOURLY; Requisition Number: REQ_753855; Location: 71338; Candidate Number: 47982098. The offer expressly states: 'All offers are conditional upon successful completion of pre-employment screening, including rehire eligibility, prior contact with internal security, and where applicable, criminal history screening.' Concurrently with the offer, on May 28, 2026 at 12:57 PM PDT, Defendant Macy's initiated a background check through vendor HireRight, LLC, Request #: OR-052826-TD9W3, Package: Package #1 - BGC - 49 States. Macy's explicitly designated this as 'Macy's Corporate Services (Pre-Employment - BGC).' The HireRight report (dated May 28–May 29, 2026) contains the following key elements: (1) SSN Validation: Complete — SSN issued in Nevada between 2010 and 2011; meets company standards. (2) SS Trace: Complete — Data Found; meets company standards. (3) Court Records: Six subrequests for Criminal & Offense History spanning San Joaquin County (CA), Sheridan County (WY), and prior residences; most remain pending; where completed (Sheridan, WY), results show 'Complete - No Court Record Found' and 'Meets Company Standards.' (4) Widescreen Plus National Criminal Search: Completed. (5) National Sex Offender Registry: Status PENDING. However, HireRight's internal comments dated May 29, 2026 3:56 PM PDT explicitly state: 'S Arun - Note: APPLICANT IS LISTED ON THE SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY IN THE STATE OF CA.' On May 29, 2026 at 3:57 PM PDT, HireRight's internal note states: 'Verified by Aka Name, DOB and Address.' On May 29, 2026 at 3:57 PM PDT, HireRight included a mandatory statutory warning: 'Information from the California Sex Offenders' Registry may not be used for employment purposes except to protect a person at risk. See CA Penal Code Section 290.46. Only use this information to make an employment decision as expressly allowed by CA law.' This explicit statutory disclaimer was included in the HireRight report delivered to Macy's. On May 29, 2026 at 4:04 PM PDT, HireRight placed a 'Delay' notation: 'Reason: Additional Research is Required to Complete This Request — Estimated Completion Date: 03-Jun-2026.' Despite the pending status and pending research completion, the report was marked 'Managed Adjudication 3.0: Pending.' The adjudication results summary shows: 'National Sex Offender Registry: In Progress, Undefined' — meaning Macy's had no finalized determination of whether the registry information met its hiring standards. Critically, the criminal court records across all four jurisdictions (San Joaquin CA, Sheridan WY, and prior addresses) showed no criminal convictions — all returned 'Clear,' 'No Court Record Found,' or 'Meets Company Standards.' Macy's received the HireRight report containing these findings: (a) zero criminal convictions in any jurisdiction; (b) explicit statutory warning that registry information cannot be used for employment purposes except to protect a person at risk; (c) notation that the final determination ('Managed Adjudication 3.0') was still pending. Plaintiff accepted the offer and commenced employment on the specified start date of May 28, 2026. ACTUAL OUTCOME (supersedes the anticipated-adverse-action theory below, which was the working hypothesis at the time this record was first drafted): Macy's Managed Adjudication 3.0 process never issued a Post-Adverse Action Notice or any registry-based rejection. Plaintiff worked the 'Captain, Selling and Support' position at the Stockton Sherwood store on a regular schedule through his last shift on July 2, 2026, per the Macy's shift records and manager text exchanges with Leticia Villarreal logged under Matter 30 — the same day CDCR's retaliatory transfer of Plaintiff's parole supervision to the Santa Clara GPS Unit (ordered June 29, 2026; see Matter 30) made the Stockton job inaccessible, prompting an LOA rather than a termination. No PC §290.46(j) violation, wrongful termination, or adverse action of any kind occurred at Macy's; the loss of this job is pled as damages in Matter 30 (CDCR/Moua retaliation), not here. This matter is retained in the portfolio only as a historical record of the BGC/registry-flag pattern that was anticipated but did not occur — the analysis below (drafted May 29, 2026, before the actual outcome was known) is preserved for that reason and should not be read as describing a live or viable claim. IMPORTANT CROSS-REFERENCE: because the theory here never materialized, Macy's is not actually a same-kind data point in the 'sixth employer' willfulness pattern asserted in Matters 27 and 29 — those entries should be read with that caveat.
